device.name: Canary Sense
device.tagline: 60 GHz radar presence — knows someone's there, never who.
device.status: phase 2 complete — signing witness, bench items open

radar.soc: ADT6101P — 2T2R antenna, 1 MB flash, on-chip Cortex-M3 DSP
radar.vitals_accuracy: breathing ~90%, heart rate ~85% (≤1.5 m, single target)
radar.link: UART1 · host TX GPIO16 → radar RX, host RX GPIO17 ← radar TX · 115200 8N1
peripherals: BH1750 ambient light (I2C SDA 22 / SCL 23, addr 0x23, 1–65,535 lux)

protocol.header: SOF(1) + frame id(2) + payload len(2) + frame type(2) + header checksum(1) — header scalars BIG-endian
protocol.payload: N payload bytes (every multi-byte payload field LITTLE-endian) + 1 data checksum byte
protocol.checksum: XOR-fold every covered byte into an 8-bit accumulator, then invert (c ^= b; c = ~c)
protocol.aggregation: each UART frame carries ONE scalar; the parser folds the latest of each into a combined snapshot for the FSMs
protocol.resync: on any checksum/length failure the parser drops a single byte and re-hunts — it never discards bytes that might start a real frame

radar.privacy: the raw radar IQ never leaves the radar module's own DSP — the host MCU only ever sees pre-digested scalars over UART: presence flag, target count, distance, breathing rate, heart rate. No camera, no microphone, no MAC surface.
radar.blackbox_note: the radar module's own firmware (in-radar zone config etc.) is partnership-gated; SecuraCV treats it as a fixed black-box claim source and does all tuning host-side on the ESP32-C6.

states.name: Unknown
states.meaning: startup, or the radar UART silent past the stall deadline — radar-link health, not a witness event

states.name: Clear
states.meaning: no target — the room reads empty

states.name: Present
states.meaning: a target sustained past the debounce — someone is here

presence.stall_note: deadline checks run BEFORE data guards: a silent radar drives the FSM to Unknown instead of freezing on the last good frame

vitals.single_target_rule: vitals are hard-suppressed unless exactly one target is present — multi-person BPM attribution is the design doc's own risk table entry
vitals.non_diagnostic: wellbeing signals, not medical data: never sealed-logged, never precise-timestamped, P1 opt-in for BPM numerics

identify.pattern: 2 Hz white flash — unmistakable against the steady presence colors

provisioning.intro: No captive portal on this witness — the Sense kit has no HTTP server at all (smaller attack surface, smaller firmware). You provision it once over USB; NVS remembers everything across every update after that.

trackb.title: Or: the 10-minute on-ramp (stock kit, zero flashing)
trackb.body: The kit ships pre-flashed with ESPHome (the upstream seeed_mr60bha2 component) speaking the ESPHome native API to Home Assistant — not MQTT. Two config-only bridges get its claims into the SecuraCV kernel:

paths.name: HA MQTT Statestream (kit stays unmodified)
paths.how: enable HA's built-in mqtt_statestream; HA republishes the kit's entities to MQTT and the mqtt_sensor adapter's mr60bha2 profile maps them into claims

paths.name: ESPHome mqtt: overlay (one OTA, no custom firmware)
paths.how: add an mqtt: block to the kit's ESPHome config and push it over the air; the device then publishes to the broker directly

trackb.honesty: Track B claims are kernel-signed at ingest, not device-signed — Home Assistant renders them with the yellow 'adapter-attested' badge, never the green 'device-verified ✓'. Track A (this page's path) earns the green badge.

use_cases.title: Restricted-zone witness
use_cases.how: ceiling/wall mount; the presence FSM emits signed PresenceInRestrictedZone claims with coarse time buckets
use_cases.why: works in total darkness where a camera can't, and indoors where WiFi-CSI is noisy — HVAC airflow doesn't affect radar

use_cases.title: After-hours corroboration
use_cases.where: paired with a camera / canary-vision zone
use_cases.how: radar presence + camera person-detection in the same time bucket = a two-physics corroborated event
use_cases.why: much stronger evidentiary weight — and a contradiction (camera says person, radar says empty) surfaces as an anomaly worth flagging

use_cases.title: Wellbeing / welfare check
use_cases.how: 'breathing confirmed within bucket' as a P0 binary; BPM numerics under P1 opt-in
use_cases.why: witnessing that a person is alive and present without a camera in a bedroom — a deployment the vision canary can never ethically serve

use_cases.title: Tamper enrichment
use_cases.how: BH1750 lux: a sudden lights-out while presence persists feeds the tamper-type sensors
use_cases.why: the radar keeps seeing when someone kills the lights — the two signals disagree exactly when something is wrong

use_cases.title: Sleep / quiet-hours baseline
use_cases.how: presence + breathing-lock scalars feed the existing anomaly-baseline pattern
use_cases.why: unusual-motion / unusual-breathing dashboards with zero new infrastructure

mounts.name: Wall / shelf — the presence workhorse
mounts.height: 1.2–2 m high, radar face level and square to the room
mounts.aim: point the antenna face at the zone you care about; the sector covers most of a room from a corner
mounts.range: static presence: 6 m on the spec sheet, ~4 m effective per Seeed's own v1.6.12 troubleshooting doc — plan zones on 4

mounts.name: Over the bed — Seeed's official vitals install
mounts.height: 1 m above the head of the bed, tilted 45° down toward the middle of the bed
mounts.aim: radar-to-chest ≤1.5 m, boresight at the torso; the vitals CORE zone is 0.5–1.5 m (outside it readings freeze or zero). Seeed recommends vitals during sleep only — not at a desk, not during exercise
mounts.range: tracking >96% at 0.5–1.5 m, >90% at 1.5–3 m, degraded 3–5 m
mounts.best_for: wellbeing builds — the welfare-check deployment; the repo ships a printable bedside stand

mounts.name: Ceiling — the fall-detection sibling's home
mounts.height: 2.2–3.0 m, facing straight down, ~2 m sensing radius
mounts.aim: that spec belongs to the MR60FDA2 fall kit (same protocol family, different radar firmware — cross-flashing bricks it); the BHA2 prefers wall/bedside
mounts.best_for: noted here so you don't ceiling-mount a BHA2 expecting FDA2 behavior

radome.rule: anything in front of the antenna must be a thin, flat, uniform, non-metal membrane — no ribs, no labels, no paint blobs over the antenna zone
radome.why: 60 GHz has ~5 mm wavelength; ribs and thickness steps in front of the antenna refract and reflect the beam
radome.repo_note: the repo's printable RADOME enclosure computes and asserts the membrane air gap in the OpenSCAD model — print it in plain PLA/PETG, never with metallic/carbon-fill filament

geometry.note: the near/mid/far bands are the firmware's own range gates (host-side zone gating) — raw centimeters never leave the device
geometry.fov_flag: Seeed's own numbers disagree: the mmWave comparison table says 120°×100° (presence) while the module datasheet says an 80°×80° sector (vitals). The lab below draws the conservative 80° — treat the extra width as bonus, never as budget

avoid.what: fans, A/C, swaying curtains and plants
avoid.why: micro-movement is motion to FMCW radar — officially acknowledged, and the #1 community false-positive; wind through a window makes curtains a permanent occupant

avoid.what: large metal surfaces and mirrors in-beam
avoid.why: radar mirrors — reflections fold ghost targets (or the next room) into your zone

avoid.what: glass or thin wooden panels between radar and room
avoid.why: Seeed explicitly says do not rely on through-glass/through-panel detection; at 60 GHz (an O₂ absorption band) every wall is a hard boundary — which is also why it never leaks into the neighbor's flat

avoid.what: another mmWave radar installed close by
avoid.why: two 60 GHz emitters raise each other's noise floor — officially listed interference
the radar can't tell its own motion from the room's; water films and flow scatter the beam — both on Seeed's official list
on Seeed's official interference list — a noisy 5 V rail degrades the radar front-end; budget 5 V/1 A clean

tuning.goal: maximum detection, minimum error — every knob below is a LIVE host-side number now (the radar module itself stays a black box): NVS-backed, tunable from Home Assistant's number entities (cfg/*/set), and bakeable as a room preset in the browser flasher. The compiled value seeds the first boot.

knobs.name: present_debounce_ms
knobs.does: how long a target must persist before Present fires
knobs.raise_when: a doorway clip or a passing pet flickers presence — 500–800 ms ignores sub-second transients
knobs.lower_when: you need instant hallway reaction and can tolerate blips

knobs.name: clear_timeout_ms
knobs.does: how long with no target before Clear fires
knobs.raise_when: a sitting person occasionally drops out — 5–10 s hold keeps still-presence latched (the classic mmWave 'holds through stillness' advantage)
knobs.lower_when: you want fast vacancy for lighting automations

knobs.name: stall_timeout_ms
knobs.does: no UART frame at all before the state goes Unknown and the radar_link problem sensor trips
knobs.raise_when: never much — 5 s already tolerates parser resync bursts

knobs.name: near_cm / mid_cm
knobs.does: the range-band gates — the host-side stand-in for in-radar zone config
knobs.raise_when: your zone of interest is deep (a long room): push mid_cm out so 'far' means 'outside my zone'
knobs.lower_when: you only care about close approach (a cabinet, a doorway)

knobs.name: vitals lock/lost (wellbeing)
knobs.does: sustained plausible vitals before the breathing lock confirms; loss window before it drops
knobs.raise_when: restless sleepers flap the lock — a longer lost window rides through position changes
knobs.lower_when: clinical-adjacent alerting where you want fast loss-of-signal notice (remember: non-diagnostic)

knobs.name: plausibility bands
knobs.does: BPM outside these bands is rejected as noise before it can reach the lock FSM

errors.reality: 60 GHz radar sees any moving mass — a cat IS a target, and the module exposes no pet-height zone or sensitivity config at all (closed firmware). A cat sleeping inside the 1.5 m vitals bubble can even produce vitals readings — small-animal breathing is within the detectable band.
errors.fix: placement + physics: mount high aiming level so a floor cat skims the cone's edge, gate on range band, and corroborate high-stakes automations with a second signal (lux, contact, a CSI Canary). The firmware's plausibility bands reject most feline heart rates from locking as a human.

errors.reality: officially acknowledged, with a documented signature: fans can make the radar report a NON-ZERO HEART RATE while breathing reads 0 and no target is detected — a phantom pulse with no lungs
errors.fix: aim the cone away first; then trust vitals only when presence is on AND breathing > 0 — the firmware's plausibility gate plus the sit-still lock already encode that sanity filter

errors.reality: presence from the hallway folded into the bedroom via a mirror is a classic; ghost targets at impossible ranges are the tell
errors.fix: re-aim so no large specular surface is in-beam; range-band gating trims ghosts beyond your zone

errors.reality: official tracking numbers: >96% at 0.5–1.5 m, >90% at 1.5–3 m, occasional target loss at 3–5 m. Radar-module firmware matters: v1.6.12 fixed stationary-target loss inside 1.5 m — the #1 'presence drops while I sit still' fix is a module firmware update
errors.fix: one device per ~4 m zone (the effective figure), keep the radar firmware current, and let clear_timeout ride through brief dropouts

errors.reality: 60 GHz penetrates blankets usefully, but a metal shelf is a wall — and Seeed says don't rely on detection through even glass or thin wood
errors.fix: mount above furniture lines; never behind a TV, appliance, or glass door

errors.cause: vitals with 2+ people in the cone
errors.reality: the radar reports ONE breath/heart estimate — with two people it's an attribution lottery. Seeed's own validity conditions demand exactly one, completely still person; occupant counting (up to 3) is officially 'experimental… a rough estimation'
errors.fix: the firmware refuses to play: vitals are hard-suppressed unless the count bucket is exactly 1 (a code rule, not advice)

errors.cause: stale vitals beyond the core zone
errors.reality: the documented trap: beyond ~1.5 m the module FREEZES breath/heart at the last valid value rather than nulling — a dashboard can show a heartbeat for an empty chair. (Stock ESPHome also skips zero-valued frames, compounding it.)
errors.fix: canary-sense publishes BPM as null the moment the lock drops — the freeze can't reach Home Assistant. On stock firmware, gate vitals on distance 50–150 cm and target count == 1 yourself

errors.reality: the 85% claim deserves context: community verdict is 'trend indicator, not a monitor' — readings rarely leave the 60–100 bpm band, one forum bench measured breathing consistently +4 BPM high, and Seeed's own v1.6.12 notes admit the vitals algorithm 'had fundamental issues' pending an ML rework
errors.fix: treat BPM as a wellbeing trend (the firmware already labels it non-diagnostic, P1-gated, never sealed-logged); the breathing LOCK binary is the signal to build on

playbook: Pick the job first: presence witness (wall, whole room) or wellbeing (over the bed, 0.5–1.5 m core zone). One device rarely does both well from one spot.
Mount square and solid: level antenna face, rigid mount, clean 5 V/1 A power, nothing in front but the radome membrane.
Update the radar module firmware to current (v1.6.12 fixed stationary-target loss) — it's a separate firmware from the host's, flashed once over a UART passthrough.
Walk the cone: use the lab pattern below on the real device — walk the room edges watching range bands flip; what you can't flip, the radar can't see.
Kill the movers: fans, curtains, dangling plants out of beam before touching any threshold.
Then tune debounce/clear to your room's rhythm — raw radar asserts in ~1 s and clears in ~5 s; the firmware's debounce/clear knobs shape that, and thresholds are for the last 10%, not the first 90%.
For automations that act (locks, alerts), corroborate: radar + lux, radar + contact, or two Canaries of different physics.

reality.title: The reality check — what the spec sheet won't tell you

flags.reality: Seeed's v1.6.12 troubleshooting doc says ~4 m effective; one reviewer measured useful distance readings capping at 2–3 m
Seeed's comparison table says 120°×100°, the datasheet says 80°×80° — the numbers disagree; design for 80°
band-limited ~60–100 bpm in practice; 'entertainment-grade' is the community verdict — a trend, not telemetry
usable as a trend; one metronome-controlled bench measured a consistent +4 BPM offset
counts up to 3, officially experimental — which is exactly why the firmware buckets it to 0/1/2+ and never publishes a precise count

sandbox.label: Walk into the room
sandbox.blurb: A target sustains past the 300 ms debounce → Present; the LED goes green and a signed event chains.

sandbox.label: Walk toward it
sandbox.blurb: Range band steps far → mid → near as you close in — the host-side zone gate in action; raw centimeters never publish.

sandbox.label: Sit still and breathe (wellbeing)
sandbox.blurb: Plausible vitals sustain 4000 ms with exactly one target → the breathing lock confirms; BPM numerics go live (P1).

sandbox.label: A second person walks in
sandbox.blurb: The count bucket moves 1 → 2+; occupancy_changed chains, and vitals hard-suppress (BPM → null) — attribution refused, by code.

sandbox.label: Everyone leaves
sandbox.blurb: No target for 1500 ms → Clear; the LED goes blue and presence_cleared chains.

sandbox.label: Kill the lights — with someone inside
sandbox.blurb: Lux collapses while radar presence persists: the tamper-corroboration pattern. Camera-blind means nothing to a radar.
sandbox.ha: lights-out + presence — the tamper automation's trigger pair

sandbox.label: Unplug the radar UART
sandbox.blurb: No frame for 5000 ms → Unknown (amber LED); the radar_link problem sensor trips. Health, not a witness event — silence is never evidence.

sandbox.label: Press Identify in Home Assistant
sandbox.blurb: The WS2812 flashes white at 2 Hz for 10 s and the identify echo mirrors the window — the 'which device is which' moment.
